memory_candidates.content: When re-verifying a task-description premise before implementing it (e.g. 'no shared X mechanism exists to adopt'), grep for the mechanism directly rather than trusting the premise -- in this codebase, context/contracts/*.md already existed as a shared hard-mode contract-text store, referenced by path from every -hard consumer, contradicting the task description's claim that it needed to be built. Verifying premises during implementation (not just during research/planning) catches drift between when a task was authored and when it is executed.

When auditing a command's flag surface for a consolidation/collapse design, check the command's own Options table directly rather than assuming flags documented elsewhere (in other files, in prose) are actually wired. In this codebase /orchestrate's own Options table lacked --fast, --team, --hard, and all four model flags entirely, despite scattered documentation implying partial support -- the correct A6 classification was REBUILD-REQUIRED for six mechanisms, not the two the task description anticipated.
